solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Badger editor to go in for basic principles

indicators.note: one piece is told to go in, entering the other so that it sits inside it

blocks.note: brock is an old country name for the badger
standard abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: An animal and a journalist are told to start at the very foundations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badger' looks like a verb meaning pester, but here it is the animal, known in the countryside as a brock.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedrock is the solid rock beneath soil, used figuratively for the fundamental ideas on which everything rests.

clue.text: Move on time to produce financial statement

blocks.note: to budge is to shift slightly
T for time, placed on (after) the first piece

explanation.surface: A finance minister is urged to get a move on with the annual statement.
explanation.definitionFit: The Budget is the UK Chancellor's yearly statement of planned taxes and spending.

clue.text: US state using pink paper for a type of glazed pottery

indicators.note: the state's name is using something new, putting it into service in place of a letter
'X for Y' means X stands in place of Y, so one letter is swapped out

blocks.note: Delaware, the first state of the USA
the Financial Times is printed on pink paper
the letter removed, signalled by 'for'

explanation.surface: An American state uses salmon-coloured paper for wrapping its glazed pots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Using pink paper for a' means the FT replaces one A in the state's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Delftware is tin-glazed earthenware, often blue and white, first made in the Dutch town of Delft.

clue.text: Natural, as no cigar can be

indicators.note: saying the words can be something else invites rearranging their letters into it

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A claim that cigars, being plant leaf, are wholesome and unprocessed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can be' says the letters of the two words may become another word.
explanation.definitionFit: Organic produce is grown without artificial chemicals, so it is natural.

clue.text: Blood relation ma is known to reform

indicators.note: to reform is to form again, so the letters are reshaped into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A mother has a reputation for mending the ways of her family.
explanation.definitionFit: A kinswoman is a female relative, related by birth.

clue.text: Tool provided by supporter of Burmese, perhaps?

blocks.note: a Burmese is a breed of cat; read as possessive, 'of Burmese' is the cat's
an animal stands on its feet, so a foot supports it

explanation.surface: A puzzling question about what a Burmese person might provide as a tool.
explanation.walkthrough: Burmese suggests a nationality, but it is a breed of cat; the cat's foot holds it up.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat's-paw is a person used as a dupe or instrument by another, from the fable of the monkey and the chestnuts.

clue.text: Ambassador and son involved in court case

indicators.note: pieces involved in something are caught up within it, so they sit inside it

blocks.note: CT is the abbreviation for court
His Excellency, the title of an ambassador
S for son

explanation.surface: A diplomat and his son are caught up in a lawsuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court case' reads as one legal phrase; 'case' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A chest is a large box or case for storing things.

clue.text: Winged sandals in unfinished story and song

indicators.note: an unfinished word lacks its ending, so its final letter is dropped

blocks.note: tale missing its final letter
an aria is a song in an opera

explanation.surface: Magic flying footwear features in an incomplete legend and a ballad.
explanation.definitionFit: The talaria are the winged sandals worn by Hermes, or Mercury, in classical myth.

clue.text: One found in place a universal spicy dish

indicators.note: something found in a place lies inside it, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names
the Roman numeral for one
taken as written
U is the film certificate meaning suitable for all

explanation.surface: Someone discovers a dish of spices that is enjoyed everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilau is rice cooked in stock with spices, a dish also called pilaf.

clue.text: Pay park keeper initially accepted, bringing ruin

indicators.note: initially points to the start of the word, so only its opening letter is kept
what is accepted is taken in, so those pieces go inside the word for pay

blocks.note: a wage is pay
rec, short for recreation ground, is a public park
first letter of keeper

explanation.surface: A park warden's salary being taken on leads to financial disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Wreckage is the remains of something destroyed, a ruin in the sense of what is left.

clue.text: Old coach's assiduity

blocks.note: first meaning: a French public stagecoach of former times
second meaning: careful, persistent effort

explanation.surface: A former sports trainer is praised for being hard-working.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining the two meanings; 'coach' suggests a trainer, but it is a horse-drawn vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Diligence means steady industrious care, and it was also the name for a continental stagecoach.

clue.text: Unhealthy entering the French industrial city

indicators.note: a word entering another goes into it and ends up surrounded by it

blocks.note: le is the French masculine for 'the'
ill means sick or unwell

explanation.surface: Something unwholesome getting into a French manufacturing town.
explanation.definitionFit: Lille is a major manufacturing and textile centre in northern France, near the Belgian border.

clue.text: Dined in steakhouse at Enfield

indicators.note: the answer is said to be in the following words, lying within their letters

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word, the middle word and the start of the town

explanation.surface: Someone had a meal at a grill restaurant in a north London suburb.
explanation.walkthrough: Enfield is a suburb in north London.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are past participle forms describing a meal having been consumed: 'having dined' and 'having eaten'.

clue.text: Antelope we track but briefly, running wild

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the word just before it loses its last letter
letters running wild are out of control, so they are jumbled into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
the word cut short by one letter

explanation.surface: Hunters follow an antelope's trail, though only for a short while, as the animal bolts.
explanation.definitionFit: The waterbuck is a large African antelope that lives near rivers and lakes.

clue.text: Compliant, as one's landlord will be

blocks.note: first meaning: obliging and willing to fit in with others
second meaning, playful: a landlord provides somewhere to live

explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning hopes the landlord is obliging, but really it is that he supplies rooms.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means helpful and easy-going, and also literally providing lodging, which is a landlord's business.

clue.text: Perceptive old boy, one below stairs, perhaps

blocks.note: OB is the abbreviation for a former pupil
domestic staff in big houses worked below stairs

explanation.surface: A sharp-eyed former pupil now works as a domestic below stairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Below stairs' is the British phrase for the servants' quarters of a large house.
explanation.definitionFit: Observant means quick to notice things, which is what perceptive describes.

clue.text: Repetitious new rite, with musical backing

indicators.note: a new version of a word is a remade one, its letters put in another order
backing suggests going backwards, so the musical's name is read from its end

blocks.note: the word rearranged
Evita is the Lloyd Webber musical about Eva Perón

explanation.surface: A fresh ceremony is accompanied by a musical score, played over and over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Musical backing' looks like accompaniment, but it says to read a musical's name backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Iterative means done again and again, each pass repeating the last.

clue.text: Old Russians in tutus regularly adopting Indian garments

indicators.note: taking letters regularly means at even intervals, here every other one
adopting something means taking it in, so the garments go inside the kept letters

blocks.note: first, third and fifth letters of tutus
saris are wrapped garments worn by Indian women

explanation.surface: Russian ballet dancers of old swap their tutus for Indian dress.
explanation.definitionFit: Tsarists were supporters of the Russian Tsar, a faction of the old imperial regime.

clue.text: Way Essex town's character is an aid to progress

blocks.note: abbreviation for street
Epping is a market town in Essex
taken as written
the character of a place or piece is its tone

explanation.surface: The feel of a road in an Essex town helps its improvement.
explanation.walkthrough: Essex is an English county east of London.
explanation.definitionFit: A stepping stone is a stone for crossing water, used figuratively for any stage that helps one advance.

clue.text: Work up new argument for bishop of Rome

indicators.note: in a down entry, working up means reading the word from bottom to top

blocks.note: op, short for opus, is a work
N for new
a tiff is a petty quarrel

explanation.surface: Someone stirs up a fresh dispute on behalf of the Pope.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'up' means read from bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: The pontiff is the Pope, whose title includes Bishop of Rome.

clue.text: Instrument in old vehicle in African capital

indicators.note: a capital is a head or top letter, so only the word's first letter is kept

blocks.note: O for old
a car is a vehicle
taken as written
the capital (first) letter of African

explanation.surface: A musical instrument travels in a battered car around an African capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'African capital' wants to be a city such as Accra; it means only the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocarina is a small egg-shaped wind instrument with finger holes.

clue.text: Prohibition covering some tropical tree

indicators.note: one word covering another wraps around it, holding it inside

blocks.note: a ban is a prohibition
any can mean some, as in 'have you any?'

explanation.surface: A ban on felling protects part of a tropical forest.
explanation.definitionFit: The banyan is an Indian fig tree whose aerial roots grow down to form extra trunks.

clue.text: Run a bar, pushing back high-class storyteller

indicators.note: pushing something back moves it further along, so one letter shifts position towards the end

blocks.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
taken as written
a counter is the bar where drinks are served
U means upper-class, a crossword convention

explanation.surface: Someone who runs a pub drives off a posh teller of tales.
explanation.walkthrough: The U in the word for a bar is shifted further back, two places towards the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A raconteur is a person who tells anecdotes skilfully and entertainingly.

clue.text: Greek island my favourite uncle originally used

indicators.note: originally means at the origin, so each word gives only its first letter

blocks.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like 'my!'
the opening letters of each word

explanation.surface: A favourite uncle used to go to a particular Greek island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' looks possessive but is an exclamation, matching the British 'cor'.
explanation.definitionFit: Corfu is a Greek island in the Ionian Sea off the north-west coast.

clue.text: Diplomat's covetousness involving ring

indicators.note: a word involving another wraps it up within itself

blocks.note: envy is wanting what others have
the letter O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: An ambassador's greed extends to wanting a ring.
explanation.definitionFit: An envoy is a messenger or representative sent on a diplomatic mission.

clue.text: Question a graduate at a Middle Eastern port

blocks.note: the second 'a', which the rest is placed at
Q is the abbreviation for question
the first 'a', taken as written
Bachelor of Arts, a first degree

explanation.surface: Someone quizzes a university graduate at a Middle Eastern port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At a' places the first three pieces after a single A.
explanation.definitionFit: Aqaba is Jordan's only seaport, on the Gulf of Aqaba at the northern tip of the Red Sea.

clue.text: Caravan mostly reputed to carry eastern king

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the word loses its final letter
to carry something is to hold it, so those letters go inside

blocks.note: said, as in 'it is said', missing its last letter
E for east
R for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A travelling group is said, for the most part, to be transporting an oriental monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Serai is short for caravanserai, the roadside inn where travelling caravans rest, and is used for the caravan itself.

clue.text: Woman with skill and practicality

blocks.note: Vi is a woman's name, short for Violet
ability is skill or talent

explanation.surface: A woman who is both able and practical.
explanation.definitionFit: Viability is the capacity of a plan to work in practice, its feasibility.

clue.text: Merry southern youth leader concealing tuft of hair

indicators.note: a leader comes first, so only the word's opening letter is taken
concealing means hiding inside, so the hair goes within the other letters

blocks.note: S for south
a quiff is a tuft of hair brushed up at the front
first letter of youth

explanation.surface: A cheerful young leader from the south hides his upswept hairstyle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Merry' is British slang for slightly drunk, not just cheerful.
explanation.definitionFit: Squiffy is British informal for slightly tipsy, as is merry in that sense.

clue.text: Part payment a German offered after dash from east

indicators.note: in an across entry, coming from the east means reading right to left
after says the German word comes later, placed behind the other piece

blocks.note: to dart is to dash
ein is German for 'a'

explanation.surface: A German person offers part of a sum after rushing in from the east.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue, reading from the east means right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade-in is an old item handed over as part of the price of a new one.
